name: Retail
blurb: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation at volume, with NRF, Coresight, and IHL tracking the deployments.

points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

summary: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation are the volume use cases.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey provides the measured adoption figure for retail trade, NAICS 44-45. In the latest period, 16.5% of retail firms answered yes to using AI in the last two weeks, up from 15.5% in the prior period. The question was first asked in September 2023, and the series is updated fortnightly. This remains a minority share of the sector.

National Retail Federation coverage points to store automation, inventory computer vision, and customer-experience software as the main retail AI applications, and its Paris conversations framed practical AI, connected stores, and relationship-driven loyalty as current priorities. IHL Group's reporting shows deployments across supply chain and store operations. GE Appliances uses autonomous vehicles, robotics, AI cameras and sensors, and its Brilliant Factory data platform at a Georgia plant to detect defects, predict equipment failures, optimize staffing, and forecast demand. Nature's Emporium uses Retailgrid's AI-powered spreadsheet and Price Radar platform to integrate daily sales data, model demand and price elasticity, and track competitors including Amazon.ca. Rainbow's Shenzhen supermarket uses 17,000 IoT devices, NexConnect Smart Carts, Nebular Ultra ESLs, AI vision, robotics, and retail AI for navigation, fulfilment, shelf execution, and replenishment. Dr. Squatch uses AfterShip's AI-powered estimated delivery dates and AfterShip Intelligence on tracking pages for delivery visibility and personalized recommendations.

IHL Group's 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, in cooperation with Chain Store Age, finds inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards. IHL Group also finds most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first, stalling AI pilots before they reach the store floor. Inventory distortion is down to $1.7 trillion, but empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion. Vendor activity spans pricing through Retailgrid, store digital twins and IoT through Hanshow and Lingzhi Digital Technology, and post-purchase tracking through AfterShip. Coresight Research, which focuses on retail and technology and has deep expertise in China, is cited as producing adoption rates and market sizing for AI in merchandising and supply-chain logistics, and it runs an invite-only forum on AI opportunities and challenges for consumer-focused businesses.

On ROI, Dr. Squatch achieved a 31.89% recommendation click-through rate, attributed $32,978 in Q1 revenue, cut WISMO inquiries 25%, and reached 94% delivery-date accuracy with AfterShip's tools. GE Appliances reports qualitative returns in the form of reduced downtime and scrap. IHL Group's finding that inventory data accuracy separates winners from laggards suggests returns depend on data quality rather than the size of an AI budget. No other retail-specific ROI percentages appear in the excerpts.

The excerpts do not quote a specific AI regulatory rule for retail. NRF's role includes standing up for policies and ideas that help retail thrive, but no AI-specific regulation is detailed. IHL Group identifies a practical risk: most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first, and pilots stall before reaching the store floor. Coresight Research's forum is described as exploring opportunities and challenges, but the excerpt does not enumerate those challenges.

A retailer deciding whether to deploy should note that measured adoption is still modest at 16.5%, up from 15.5%, and that the clearest reported wins come from focused operational use cases such as delivery tracking, pricing, and defect detection rather than broad AI spend. IHL Group's evidence points to inventory data accuracy as the prerequisite that separates winners from laggards, and to the risk of funding the wrong layer first. The vendor landscape is active across pricing, store operations, and post-purchase experience, but the excerpts suggest returns are tied to specific bottlenecks and data quality, not to the size of an AI budget.

https://nrf.com/.brief: The National Retail Federation describes itself as an advocate for the people, policies, and ideas that support a thriving retail sector, and it provides retail news, insights, and industry events. According to the organization, conversations held in Paris illustrated how retailers are putting what it calls "The Next Now" into practice. These efforts span practical artificial intelligence, connected stores, and loyalty programs built on relationships.

https://coresight.com/.brief: Coresight Research says it delivers data-driven insights centered on retail and technology. It also claims deep expertise in China that it describes as unique in the industry. Additionally, the firm reports leading an invite-only, collaborative forum exploring AI opportunities and challenges for consumer-focused businesses.

https://ihlservices.com/.brief: IHL Group conducts research on retail technology spending and strategy. According to their 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, inventory data accuracy rather than AI budget size determines which specialty retailers succeed, and most retail AI budgets fund the wrong infrastructure layer first. The organisation also reports that inventory distortion has declined to $1.7 trillion, though empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion annually. IHL's analysis finds that the presence of AI does not predict pricing-platform quality among vendors, and retailers should instead evaluate explainability, automation controls, and governance safeguards.
